Dear Mr. Sarly,

I forward herewith for your information tabulated
statement relating to the arrest by the Municipal Police
of a communist named Kan Ching Ming (耿敬民) alias Kan
Ching Tung (耿敬冬) at 2.20 a.m. January 11, 1934 at
House No.23, Lane No.203, Hupeh Road.

The accused appeared on remand before the Second
Branch of the Kiangsu High Court on February 5, 1934 and
was ordered to be handed over to the Chinese authorities.

Yours sincerely,

Monsieur R. Sarly,
Chief of the Political Section,
French Police Headquarters.

Judge to Mr. Tseu:—The reply of Nanchang has still not arrived at this court yet, but during the remand the Court has obtained the record from the Garrison Commander Headquarters.

Accused: I do not know Sih Ts Tsoh. I have been a business man for over twenty years and I do not know anything about political affairs.

Mr. Tseu:—I ask the accused be handed over to the S.P.S.B. because the accused is implicated by Sih Ts Tsoh. The correct address and the name of the accused mentioned in the record are enough to prove that the implications are true.

Mr. Chang:—It is undoubtedly that the accused has been a business man so far as the nature of the documents seized is concerned. Whether or not the evidence produced by the S.P.S.B. is sufficient for extradition, the Police entirely leave it to Court to decide.

Decision
Accused to be handed over to the Public Safety Bureau. (Handed over on 5/2/34.)

~~Communist Propaganda - One arrest~~
D5618
Acting on the authority of a warrant issued at the
request of the Shanghai Bureau of Public Safety, the
Municipal Police at 2.20 a.m. January 11 arrested a male
Chinese named Kan Ching-ming (耿敬民) alias Kan Ching-zung
(耿敬臣) in premises No.H.23, Lane 203, Hupeh Road.
The arrested person is wanted by the Chinese Authorities
on a charge of propagating communism. He was taken before
the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court on the morning of
January 11, when the case was remanded until January 13.

A copy of a communist handbill entitled "Open Letter
to the Chinese People in connection with the Fukien Incident",
issued by the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist
Party and dated December 13, 1933, was obtained by the
Municipal Police on January 10, 1934, in Western Chapel.
This document characterizes the "People's Revolutionary
Government" of Fukien as a camouflaged reactionary regime
and calls upon the toiling masses of Fukien to arm
themselves against Japanese Imperialism and to demand the
retrocession of the Japanese Concession at Foochow.

政治 (3)

~~共产党宣传 - 逮捕一人~~
D5618
根据应上海公安局要求签发的搜查令授权，
公共租界警务处于1月11日凌晨2时20分，在湖北路203弄H.23号 premises 逮捕了一名中国男子，名叫耿敬民（Kan Ching-ming），别名耿敬臣（Kan Ching-zung）。
该被捕者因散布共产主义罪名被中国当局通缉。他于1月11日上午被提审至江苏高等法院第二分院，案件被还押至1月13日。

公共租界警务处于1934年1月10日在西教堂（Western Chapel）获得了一份题为《关于福建事变致中国人民的公开信》的共产党传单副本，由中国共产党中央委员会发布，日期为1933年12月13日。该文件将福建的“人民革命政府”定性为伪装的反动政权，并号召福建劳苦大众武装起来反对日本帝国主义，并要求收回福州的日本租界。
